Hi Michael,

Thanks for the call this morning. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of constraints we need to see reflected in the SLA template before we can proceed to formal review:

1) A baseline monthly uptime commitment of 99.90% across production endpoints.
2) A clear monthly remediation mechanism with a cap on credits (we need predictability for our finance team) and a definition of what counts toward an incident (e.g., total outage vs. partial degraded latency).
3) Explicit latency windows for API p95 under our production profile (we can share traces) and carveouts for scheduled maintenance windows.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a fixed monthly credit cap (we suggested up to 10% of monthly spend) and alternate definitions for partial degradation? If not, what alternative guardrails would you propose that still gives us financial predictability?

I attached the procurement intake checklist and our standard template for reference.

Appreciate a short reply with the options and next steps — procurement wants the redline by next Tuesday.

Best,

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Acct Exec) and Aditya (Head of Reliability) to propose an approach. Quick answers up front:

- Baseline uptime: we typically commit to 99.95% for hosted Tier-2 customers. For enterprise customers that require predictable cost bands, we can discuss a 99.90% baseline if paired with a capped monthly remediation pool.
- Credit cap: we are open to a capped remediation pool. Our standard is a pro-rata credit (up to 100% of monthly service fees in extreme scenarios). For FinServe we can offer a monthly cap at 10% of monthly invoice with a calendar-quarter aggregate cap to avoid cliff effects.
- Partial degradation: we define incidents by availability at the endpoint layer; latency degradations that still return successful responses are typically handled under a separate latency SLO with distinct credit buckets. We can outline a two-track remedy: availability credits for total unavailability, and latency credits for p95 breaches.

I will turn this over to Aditya to outline the latency thresholds and to Monica to propose precise credit language and the redline pace. Expect a redline and a supporting remediation schedule by next Monday EOD.

Best,
Michael Grant\Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: proposed SLO bands and credit mechanics for FinServe (draft)

Folks — internal draft notes before I hand off the redline:

Summary proposal (short):
- Availability SLO: 99.90% baseline (monthly). Remedy: availability credits at these tiers: 99.90–99.00: 5% credit; 99.00–95.00: 10% credit; <95.00: 20% credit. Monthly cap: 10% of monthly invoice.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 450ms for production profile. Breaches: 1–3% over p95 -> 2% credit (capped); 3–10% -> 5% credit. Separate monthly cap shared with availability (combined cap 10%).
- Incident definitions: total endpoint failure (no 200s) = availability incident. Elevated error rates but intact 200 responses = latency/error incident.
- Maintenance carveout: 60-minute scheduled maintenance per calendar month per region with 7-day notice; emergency maintenance with reasonable notice and post-event report.

Risks/notes:
- Finance/privacy wants predictability — suggest we offer a quarterly reconciliation that smooths monthly spikes (i.e., monthly cap at 10%, but we apply a quarterly cap of 20% to avoid front-loading risk).
- For very large sustained degradations we retain the right to propose remediation other than credits (service credits, engineering prioritization, accelerated throughput credits).

Attachments I will include in the outgoing redline: Redwood_SLA_Template_FinServe_Redline.pdf (redline) and Monthly_Remediation_Schedule.xlsx (credits table).

If you both sign off, Monica can send to Sarah next week with minimal edits.

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks for the patience — attached is a concise redline that reflects the options we discussed. Key points:

- Baseline availability: Redwood accepts a 99.90% monthly availability commitment for the tied production endpoints.
- Remediation mechanics: availability and latency remedies are defined separately with a combined monthly credit cap of 10% of the monthly invoice. We also propose a quarterly aggregate cap of 20% to smooth volatility.
- Definitions: the redline separates availability incidents (no successful 200s for a given CDN/API endpoint for >1 minute) from latency incidents (p95 violations over a 1-hour window measured against FinServe's production trace profile).
- Maintenance carveouts: standard scheduled windows (60 min/month/region) with notification and an emergency maintenance process.

Next steps we recommend:

2) If acceptable, we can exchange a DocuSign-ready version and propose a short pilot (60-day observation) to validate p95 thresholds using FinServe traces.
